{{nihongo|'''Toyozumi Shrine'''|豊積神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Shimizu-ku, Shizuoka|Q79385|qid=Q79385}}, {{ill|Shizuoka (city)|Q174691|qid=Q174691}}, {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|Q131320|qid=Q131320}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, the {{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}} of {{ill|Suruga Province|Q864170|qid=Q864170}}, and its former rank under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}. {{nihongo|'''Toyozumi Shrine'''|豊積神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Suruga Province]].

== Enshrined deity ==
The shrine enshrines the following one deity{{Sfn|明治神社誌料|1912年}}:
* '''{{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|Q1781862|qid=Q1781862|lt=Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto}}'''

== History ==
== Overview ==
According to shrine tradition, it was founded in {{ill|791|Q31078|qid=Q31078}} ({{ill|Enryaku|Q1373176|qid=Q1373176}} 10){{Sfn|豊積神社（平）|2000年}}. It is also said that {{ill|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|Q941979|qid=Q941979}} prayed here for victory during his eastern campaign and, on his return, dedicated kagura in celebration; the Yui Otaiko Festival (prefecturally designated intangible folk cultural property) is said to originate from that kagura<ref name="説明板">Local explanatory signboard.</ref>.

In the ''{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}'' {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}} compiled in {{ill|927|ab|927|af|927|am|927 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|927|ar|927|ary|927|ast|927|avk|927|az|927|azb|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|bar|927|bcl|927|be|927|be_x_old|927|bg|927|bn|৯২৭|bpy|মারি ৯২৭|br|927|bs|927.|ca|927|cdo|927 nièng|ceb|927|ckb|٩٢٧|crh|927|cs|927|csb|927|cv|927|cy|927|da|927|de|927|el|927|eml|927|eo|927|es|927|et|927|eu|927|fa|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|fi|927|fo|927|fr|927|fy|927|ga|927|gan|927年|gd|927|gl|927|he|927|hi|927|hr|927.|ht|927 (almanak jilyen)|hu|927|hy|927|id|927|ilo|927|io|927|is|927|it|927|ja|927年|jv|927|ka|927|kaa|927|kk|927 жыл|ko|927년|la|927|lb|927|lij|927|lmo|927|lt|927 m.|lv|927. gads|map_bms|927|mdf|927|mg|927|mhr|927|mi|927|mk|927|mr|इ.स. ९२७|mrj|927 и|ms|927|mzn|۹۲۷|nah|927|nap|927|nds|927|new|सन् ९२७|nl|927|nn|927|no|927|nrm|927|nso|927|oc|927|or|୯୨୭|os|927-æм аз|pl|927|pnb|927|pt|927|qu|927|ro|927|ru|927 год|rue|927|sa|९२७|scn|927|sd|927ع|se|927|sh|927.|shn|927|si|927|sk|927|smn|927|sq|927|sr|927|su|927|sv|927|sw|927|tg|Соли 927|th|พ.ศ. 1470|tk|927|tl|927|tly|927|tr|927|tt|927 ел|uk|927|ur|927ء|uz|927|vec|927|vi|927|war|927|wuu|927年|xmf|927|zh|927年|zh_min_nan|927 nî|zh_yue|927年|qid=Q30470}} ({{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Encho}} 5), "Toyozumi Shrine" is listed under Ihara District ({{ill|Ihara District, Shizuoka|Q988501|qid=Q988501}}), {{ill|Suruga Province|Q864170|qid=Q864170}}. This shrine is widely regarded as that listing{{Sfn|豊積神社（平）|2000年}}<ref group="注">For the Engishiki shrine "Toyozumi Shrine," another theory identifies it with Toyoyuke Shrine in Ihara-cho, Shimizu Ward, Shizuoka.</ref>.

In ''{{ill|Suruga no Kuni Fudoki|Q11668491|qid=Q11668491}}'', the entry states "Toyozumi Shrine (or Toyoyuke Shrine), place where {{ill|Yamato Takeru|Q461258|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru}} was worshipped, the Ninomiya of the province," from which it is inferred that this shrine held second rank after {{ill|Fujisan Hongū Sengen Taisha|Q653180|qid=Q653180}} (the {{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}}) in Suruga{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=151}}. However, the basis for that statement in the same text is unclear{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=151}}.

In the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}}, its stamped-land allotment was over 16 koku{{Sfn|豊積神社（平）|2000年}}. As seen in documents from {{ill|1589|Q6759|qid=Q6759}} ({{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 17), in the early modern period it was also called "Sengen"{{Sfn|豊積神社（平）|2000年}}. A petition from {{ill|1736|Q6989|qid=Q6989}} ({{ill|Kyōhō|Q1145048|qid=Q1145048}} 21) calls it "Toyozumi Sengen-sha" and claims descent from the Engishiki shrine "Toyozumi Shrine"{{Sfn|豊積神社（平）|2000年}}.

== Divine rank ==
* Junior Fifth Rank Lower (in ''Suruga no Kuni Shinmeicho''){{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=151}} - written as "Toyozumi Tenjin."

== Precincts ==
The main hall is a fully zelkova-built {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684}} structure with copper-sheet roofing<ref name="説明板"/>. Ridge tags state it was built in {{ill|1825|Q6997|qid=Q6997}} ({{ill|Bunsei|Q1327119|qid=Q1327119}} 8), and before that there were constructions in {{ill|1600|Q6720|qid=Q6720}} ({{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 5) and rebuilding in {{ill|1732|Q6966|qid=Q6966}} ({{ill|Kyōhō|Q1145048|qid=Q1145048}} 17)<ref name="説明板"/>. The roof was originally {{ill|cypress bark roof|Q90373477|qid=Q90373477}} but was changed to copper sheet in Meiji 22 ({{ill|1889|ab|1889|af|1889|als|1889|am|1889 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1889|ar|1889|ary|1889|arz|1889|ast|1889|avk|1889|az|1889|azb|۱۸۸۹ (میلادی)|ba|1889 йыл|ban|1889|bar|1889|bat_smg|1889|bcl|1889|be|1889|be_x_old|1889|bg|1889|bn|১৮৮৯|bpy|মারি ১৮৮৯|br|1889|bs|1889.|ca|1889|cdo|1889 nièng|ce|1889 шо|ceb|1889|ckb|١٨٨٩|crh|1889|cs|1889|csb|1889|cv|1889|cy|1889|da|1889|de|1889|diq|1889|el|1889|eml|1889|eo|1889|es|1889|et|1889|eu|1889|fa|۱۸۸۹|fi|1889|fiu_vro|1889|fo|1889|fr|1889|frp|1889|frr|1889|fur|1889|fy|1889|ga|1889|gan|1889年|gcr|1889|gd|1889|gl|1889|gn|1889|gv|1889|he|1889|hi|१८८९|hif|1889|hr|1889.|hsb|1889|ht|1889 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1889|hy|1889|hyw|1889 թուական|ia|1889|id|1889|ilo|1889|io|1889|is|1889|it|1889|ja|1889年|jv|1889|ka|1889|kaa|1889|kk|1889 жыл|kn|೧೮೮೯|ko|1889년|krc|1889 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1889|ku|1889|kv|1889-ӧд во|la|1889|lb|1889|lez|1889 йис|li|1889|lij|1889|lmo|1889|lt|1889 m.|lv|1889. gads|mai|१८८९|map_bms|1889|mdf|1889|mg|1889|mhr|1889|mi|1889|min|1889|mk|1889|ml|1889|mn|1889 он|mr|इ.स. १८८९|mrj|1889 и|ms|1889|my|၁၈၈၉|myv|1889 ие|mzn|۱۸۸۹|nah|1889|nap|1889|nds|1889|new|ई सं १८८९|nl|1889|nn|1889|no|1889|nov|1889|nrm|1889|nso|1889|oc|1889|olo|1889|or|୧୮୮୯|os|1889-æм аз|pa|1889|pap|1889|pl|1889|pnb|1889|pt|1889|qu|1889|ro|1889|ru|1889 год|rue|1889|sa|१८८९|sah|1889|scn|1889|sd|1889ع|se|1889|sh|1889.|shn|1889|si|1889|simple|1889|sk|1889|sl|1889|smn|1889|sq|1889|sr|1889|stq|1889|su|1889|sv|1889|sw|1889|szl|1889|ta|1889|te|1889|tet|1889|tg|Соли 1889|th|พ.ศ. 2432|tk|1889|tl|1889|tly|1889|tr|1889|tt|1889 ел|udm|1889 ар|ug|1889|uk|1889|ur|1889ء|uz|1889|vec|1889|vi|1889|vls|1889|vo|1889|wa|1889|war|1889|wuu|1889年|xmf|1889|yi|1889|za|1889 nienz|zea|1889|zh|1889年|zh_classical|一八八九年|zh_min_nan|1889 nî|zh_yue|1889年|qid=Q7831}})<ref name="説明板"/>. After major repairs in Showa 28 ({{ill|1953|Q18585|qid=Q18585}}), it reached its current form<ref name="説明板"/>.

Large {{ill|Ginkgo biloba|Q43284|qid=Q43284}} and {{ill|Camphora officinarum|Q158722|qid=Q158722}} trees also stand in the grounds.

== Subsidiary shrines ==
Precinct shrines are as follows<ref name="説明板"/>:
* Shirahige Shrine - deity: Sarutahiko deity
* Five-shrine group
** Yamamiya Shrine - deity: Oyamatsumi deity
** Hie Shrine - deities: Oyamakui-no-Mikoto, Hayasusanoo-no-Mikoto
** Suga Shrine - deity: Takesusanoo-no-Mikoto
** Inari Shrine - deity: Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto
** Isomae Shrine - deities: Okuninushi-no-Mikoto, Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto
* One-shrine group
